text:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a steady CPU/memory growth on the compatibility proxy since we turned on v5 envelopes for internal clients. Looks like the shim path is causing large KV-cache retention and a lot of per-request envelope copies.

Maria: Noted. Is this primarily the envelope->ndjson rewriter in the proxy or something in the sidecar?

Alex: Proxy. The rewriter runs in the request path to unwrap legacy payloads and mutate headers. On high concurrent short requests (embeddings/light chat) we see sustained RSS growth and GC pressure.

Devon: Any logs/metrics? can we repro with a load test?

Alex: infra-bot posted the heap dumps and flamegraphs into the incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/inc/3872. TL;DR: large allocations in `CompatibilityRewriter.rewrite()` and `EnvelopeParser.parse()` for ~40% of requests.

infra-bot: link to heap dump: s3://redwood-heapdumps/2026-03-18/compat-proxy-heap-1717204329.hprof

Anjali: Oof. That explains the latency spikes too — GC + copying. Two ideas: 1) move heavy unwrap work to async sidecar (best perf), 2) short-circuit fallback when client advertises v5 via header (fast path), or 3) implement a lightweight zero-copy unwrap for common cases.

Maria: Quick win would be (2) — add a strict `X-Client-Version` sniff that avoids rewriter entirely when present. We already have header sniffing in the router.

TJ: +1 for (2) as immediate mitigation. But we need a plan for clients that don't send the header. We can't just force them.

Devon: For an incremental rollout: (a) enable header sniffing in prod behind a feature flag, (b) add a tenant opt-in to skip rewrite, (c) land a trimmed zero-copy path for the top 3 request shapes.

Alex: Proposal: feature flag `compat_proxy_fastpath` default off. Wave 1: enable for internal tenants only, monitor memory, CPU, error rate. Wave 2: offer tenant opt-in via console + API. Wave 3: full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Maria: We should also add a circuit-breaker that rejects rewrite under sustained memory pressure, returning 429 with an explicit `Retry-After` and a `X-Compat-Reason: mem-pressure` header so clients can optionally back off or retry via dedicated endpoints.

Anjali: +monitoring checklist: peak RSS, GC pause time, per-request allocation, p50/p95 latency, rewrite hit-rate, and the ratio of zero-copy vs fallback. Also capture sample payloads causing the worst allocations.

Devon: Who owns the rollout? I'll pick up the feature flag + circuit-breaker in proxy. Alex — can you prototype the zero-copy unwrap for the 2 small envelope shapes? Anjali — can you add the eval/metric dashboards? Maria — coordinate the tenant opt-in UX with product. TJ — run a blue-green load test next week.

Alex: I'll start the zero-copy prototype today. Quick note on implementation: we can avoid allocations by parsing in-place and using slice refs for header values, but we need to audit for lifetime issues since requests cross goroutines in the pool.

Maria: If shifting unsafe slices is risky, we can instead use a small object pool to reuse buffers — less risky but might not fix GC churn entirely. Put both options in the RFC/implementation doc.

Devon: Timeline proposal: 3 days for feature flag + circuit-breaker; 5 days for zero-copy prototype; 2 days for dashboards; 1 day for tenant opt-in backend + small console tweak; 1 day for staged rollout and verification. Total ~12 working days if parallelized.

Anjali: Add an observability kill-switch: if mem or cpu exceed thresholds for 5m, auto-flip `compat_proxy_fastpath` off. That saves on-call frantic rollbacks.

TJ: I'll schedule an isolated load run on Thursday at 10am PT. We'll test with 2MM small embedding requests + variety of envelope shapes.

Alex: Quick implementation snippet I'll try: 
```
// pseudo
func unwrapInPlace(buf []byte) (headerSlice, bodySlice []byte) {
  // find envelope bounds without copying
}
```
This will be guarded behind flag and tests for pointer safety.

Devon: Also log `X-Compat-Path: fastpath|rewriter|circuit-breaker` on every request for post-hoc signal.

Maria: Good. Also, add a deprecation note in the API docs — signal to integrators that once tenants opt-in we will stop supporting legacy envelopes in 3 months. Gives them runway and encourages header adoption.

Anjali: Action items summarized: 
- Devon: feature flag + CB + request header logging (owner)
- Alex: zero-copy prototype + safety tests (owner)
- Anjali: dashboards + auto-kill-switch (owner)
- Maria: tenant opt-in design + deprecation copy (owner)
- TJ: load test run + postmortem (owner)

Alex: I'll open the implementation PR and link it here. Expect initial perf numbers in the branch.

Maria: Thanks — let's keep communication in this thread for status updates. :thumbsup:

Devon: If anyone hits a blocker ping me in #eng-oncall.

infra-bot: created ticket INC-3872 and linked PR https://git.redwood/infer/compat-proxy/compare/fastpath

Alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infer/compat-proxy/pull/412 — includes flag + basic logging.

TJ: Load test scheduled — will post results here.

Anjali: Noted. We'll also add a small orthogonal test that simulates mixed-tenancy to ensure the tenant opt-in gating behaves correctly.

Maria: Nice work everyone.
